transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Yeah, um... I finally ended up calling the employee assistance program at work. HR is always pushing that thing, you know? They have these glossy posters in the breakroom with people smiling on hikes and stuff, which always seemed kind of cheesy to me. I never thought I'd actually use it. But I called them because I’m just... I'm barely sleeping right. 

I just lie there at night replaying work, and then replaying these arguments I've been having at home. Like, as a sales manager, it's always quarter-end in my head. Just yesterday, one of my reps completely botched a pitch to a client we've been courting for six months, and I had to step in and try to salvage it. And my wife gets on my case because I bring that energy home, and we end up bickering about stupid things, like whose turn it is to take the trash out. I even bought those new heavy-duty bags last week so they wouldn't rip, but she still... anyway. 

I just lie awake thinking about all of it. Then I'll wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and that's it, I'm just up. By the time I actually have to start my day, I feel like I never really rested at all. Have you ever tried to run a sales meeting on zero sleep? It's not great.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things throughout the day, not just when you're lying awake at night?

Worrying excessively during the day? Not really, no. I mean, during the day I'm just too slammed to sit around worrying. I'm usually bouncing from one call to the next. 

Like on Tuesday, I had this back-to-back block of Zoom meetings, and my Bluetooth headset just completely died right in the middle of talking to a vendor. I had to scramble to find my old wired earbuds, you know, the ones that used to come with the old phones? They always get completely tangled in my laptop bag. I swear I spend half my life untangling cords. I actually bought one of those little leather cord organizer things online a few weeks ago, but I always forget to use it. It's just sitting on my desk right now next to a stack of expense reports I still need to approve. My reps are terrible at submitting their receipts on time, and accounting gets on my case about it. 

But, um... wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Oh, worrying. Yeah, no, I don't really notice feeling worried while I'm at work or anything. It's really just when I'm lying in bed and it's quiet that my brain won't shut off.
Do you feel tired or exhausted during the day?

Tired? I mean, yeah, definitely. When you're waking up at 3 AM every night, you're going to be dragging. I basically survive on coffee right now. 

We actually just got this ridiculously fancy espresso machine at the office. The VP of Sales insisted on it after he went to some leadership conference in Vegas. But it takes these specific little pods that are totally overpriced, and I tried ordering some knock-off ones online to save the department budget—because accounting is always breathing down my neck about quarterly expenses—but they just end up jamming the machine. It's a total disaster. Just yesterday it sprayed hot water all over Dave from marketing. He was wearing these really light beige khakis, which, honestly, who wears light khakis when it's pouring rain out? I always stick to dark navy slacks. You can spill almost anything on them and it just blends in. I actually buy them from this outlet mall upstate, they have this great deal where if you buy three... 

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, being exhausted. Yeah, I drink a ton of coffee to push through, but I'm pretty wiped out by the time the afternoon rolls around.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain things or situations because they remind you of your stress or worries?

Avoiding things? Um, no, not really. I mean, I still go to work and do what I have to do. I don't really have the luxury of avoiding things, to be honest. 

Like, if I avoided every stressful client, I wouldn't have a job. Take this one guy we deal with, Henderson. He is notoriously difficult. Every time we jump on a call with him, he wants to renegotiate the contract terms we literally just agreed on the week before. It's maddening. Last time we met him for lunch, he insisted on going to this super high-end steakhouse downtown. The parking there is a nightmare. I had to circle the block like four times and ended up parking in this garage that charged me forty bucks for two hours. Forty bucks! And the valet guy scratched my bumper. It's just a tiny scratch, but I drive a leased car, so now I have to figure out if I should try to buff it out myself or take it to a shop before I turn it in next spring. I was looking at these scratch repair kits online, the ones with the little buffing pads that attach to your drill? Have you seen those? I don't even know if they actually work or if they just ruin the clear coat. 

But anyway, yeah, I don't avoid things. I just deal with it all, even if it keeps me up at night.
Do you have bad dreams or nightmares?

Bad dreams? No, not really. I mean, when I actually manage to fall asleep, I don't really dream at all. Or at least I don't remember them if I do. 

My wife, though, she has the craziest dreams. The other morning she woke up and told me she dreamt she was trying to return a toaster to a grocery store, but the cashier was a giant talking parrot. I don't know where she comes up with this stuff. Speaking of toasters, ours has been acting up lately. You have to push the lever down like three times before it actually catches, and then half the time it burns one side of the bread and barely toasts the other. It's one of those fancy stainless steel ones, too, supposed to be top of the line. I got it on sale at Bed Bath & Beyond right before they closed all their stores. Man, I used to love those 20% off coupons they sent in the mail. I swear we had a whole drawer dedicated just to those coupons. My wife would always forget to bring them when we actually went to the store, though, which drove me crazy because then we'd pay full price for stuff like... I don't know, decorative pillows or whatever. 

But um, anyway, what were you asking? Oh, nightmares. Yeah, no, I don't really get those. Just the whole waking up at 3 AM and not being able to shut my brain off thing.
Do you have trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks during the day?

Concentrating? Yeah, it's... it's gotten pretty bad, actually. I used to be able to just knock out these sales forecasts and client decks so quickly. But lately, I'll sit there and read the same slide like five times, and I just second-guess every single number. I can't even decide what to say on the calls anymore. 

Which is a huge problem because we just switched to this new CRM software at work, Salesforce, maybe you've heard of it? It's supposed to make everything more streamlined, but the interface is just a cluttered mess. They made us sit through this three-hour training seminar on Zoom last week. Three hours! And the trainer kept having audio issues, so he sounded like he was underwater half the time. Plus, he had this really distracting background, like a fake beach with palm trees that kept glitching around his head whenever he moved. I don't get why people use those fake backgrounds. Just blur your living room if it's messy, you know? I actually set up my home office in the guest bedroom, and I made sure to position the desk so the camera just shows this nice, plain bookshelf. I even bought these little succulent plants to put on the shelves to make it look professional. But then I overwatered one of them and the pot didn't have a drainage hole, so the roots just rotted out. It smelled terrible. I had to throw the whole thing away and bleach the shelf because it left this weird water ring on the wood. 

Sorry, what was the question? Oh, focusing. Yeah, I just... I can't seem to keep my mind on my work. It's like my brain just won't lock in on anything I need to get done.
Have you experienced any significant life changes or stressors recently, apart from the work-related issues you've mentioned?

Significant life changes? No, not really. I mean, work is the main thing, like I said. Everything else is pretty much the same. Same house, same routine, same wife. 

Although, speaking of my wife, she's been on this massive decluttering kick lately. Have you seen that show on Netflix, the one with the lady who tells you to throw away anything that doesn't spark joy? Well, my wife watched like two seasons of it over the weekend, and now our house is just chaotic. I came home on Tuesday and she had literally dumped every single piece of clothing we own onto our bed. Just a massive mountain of laundry. I couldn't even find my favorite gray hoodie, the one I got at that college football game years ago. The team lost by like thirty points, it was freezing raining, and the hot chocolate they sold at the concession stand tasted like warm brown water, but it's still my favorite hoodie because it's broken in perfectly. Anyway, I guess it didn't "spark joy" for her because she put it in the donation pile. I had to sneak out to the garage and fish it out of a black trash bag before the Goodwill truck came. And the garage is a whole other story. We have these overhead storage racks that I installed myself last summer. Took me an entire weekend because the studs in our ceiling are spaced really weirdly, like 24 inches apart instead of 16. I had to buy a special stud finder that detects the density of the drywall or something. Cost me like sixty bucks at Home Depot, and I've only used it that one time. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Life changes? Yeah, no, nothing major. Just work stress, mostly.
Do you find that your worrying or stress is primarily focused on a specific area of your life, such as work?

Work? Yeah, I mean, that's definitely the biggest part of it right now. I just can't seem to get out from under it. Like I was saying with that new CRM system, it's just a constant headache. 

And my boss, Dave, he's been breathing down my neck about Q3 projections. Dave is... well, he's one of those guys who uses sports metaphors for literally everything. Every meeting is about "moving the goalposts" or "hitting it out of the park." He even brought a literal baseball bat into the conference room once and just held it while he talked. It was so weird. Like, what are you going to do, Dave, smash the whiteboard if we don't meet our quotas? And he has this weird habit of chewing on the plastic caps of his pens. He goes through a pack of those cheap Bic pens a week, just gnawing on them until they're totally mangled. I tried to buy him a nice metal pen for Secret Santa last year, you know, one of those engraved ones? I thought maybe it would stop him from chewing on them. I ordered it online from this site that does custom engraving, but I accidentally selected the font called "Comic Sans" instead of the professional one. So it arrived looking like a joke gift. I gave it to him anyway, and he actually loved it. He still uses it, but he just chews on the metal part now, which honestly sounds terrible when it scrapes against his teeth. It makes my skin crawl just thinking about it. 

But, uh, anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, worrying. Yeah, it's mostly just work. I don't really have the energy to worry about much else these days.
Have you noticed any improvement in your sleep or overall stress levels when you're on vacation or completely removed from work-related responsibilities?

Vacation? Man, I haven't taken a real vacation in... I don't even know how long. We were supposed to go to Cabo last year, but then our dog got sick. We have this golden retriever, Buster, and he ate a whole pack of sugar-free gum that my wife left in her purse on the floor. Apparently, the artificial sweetener in that stuff is super toxic to dogs. Xylitol, I think it's called? We had to rush him to the emergency vet at like two in the morning. That place was depressing, just fluorescent lights and people crying in the waiting room. The coffee from their vending machine was probably the worst I've ever had, and I've drank gas station coffee that's been sitting on the burner for six hours. Anyway, Buster had to stay there for three days on an IV. Cost us like two grand. So, the vacation fund went straight to the vet. We ended up just doing a "staycation," which is basically just sitting at home doing chores you've been putting off. I spent three days power-washing the driveway. Did you know if you hold the nozzle too close to the concrete, it actually chips away the top layer? Now I have these weird squiggly lines etched into the driveway that you can see when it rains. It drives me crazy every time I pull the car in. 

But um, sleep? Yeah, actually, that's kind of what pushed me to finally call the employee assistance program. I'm just barely sleeping right now. Even on weekends or when I'm not technically working, I just lie there in the dark. My brain is just replaying every single email, every work problem, or even just dumb arguments with my wife about the laundry. Then I'll finally drift off, but I always wake up around 3 or 4 a.m., just staring at the ceiling. And when my alarm finally goes off, I feel like I never even rested. It's just exhausting.
Do you think your sleep would improve if your work-related stress were to be significantly reduced?

Would it improve? I mean, maybe? Like I was just saying, the whole reason I finally reached out to the employee assistance program is because my sleep is just totally wrecked right now. I'm just lying there every night replaying all that work stuff, or the dumb arguments at home, waking up at 3 or 4 a.m., and then I start the next day feeling like I never even closed my eyes. So yeah, if the work stress wasn't there, maybe my brain would shut off. 

But honestly, sometimes I wonder if part of it is our mattress. We bought this memory foam one a couple of years ago. The salesman swore up and down it had this special cooling gel infused into it, like it was developed by NASA or something. He said it pulls the heat away from your body. But I swear it does the exact opposite. It's like sleeping on a giant radiator. And getting that thing into the house was a nightmare. It was one of those bed-in-a-box things, but it weighed like a hundred and fifty pounds. The delivery guy just left it on the porch. I tried to drag it upstairs myself, and I ended up putting a massive scuff mark on the wall right where the stairs turn. I tried using one of those Magic Erasers on it? But it took the actual gloss off the paint, so now there's this dull, flat patch on the wall that catches the light weirdly. My wife noticed it immediately, of course. Now she wants to repaint the entire hallway. Do you know how many shades of white paint there are at the hardware store? It’s insane. There’s 'Alabaster,' 'Swiss Coffee,' 'Navajo White'... they all just look like plain white to me, but she brought home like fifteen of those little paper swatches and taped them to the wall. 

Um... wait, sorry. You were asking if less work stress would help me sleep. Yeah, probably. If I didn't have Dave's quotas to replay in my head all night, I might actually get a few hours. Assuming I don't overheat on that stupid mattress.
Have you experienced any significant emotional or behavioral changes in response to your work stress, such as feeling hopeless or having difficulty coping?

Hopeless? I mean... yeah, kind of. Most days I feel like this heavy, gray mood just follows me around. It comes with me from the office, gets in the car with me, follows me into the house. Even when nothing specific is happening, like if I'm just sitting on the couch, I just feel kind of hollow. 

Speaking of the couch, we actually just got a new one because Buster completely ruined the old one. He has this thing where he tries to "dig" into the cushions before he lies down. My wife read somewhere that it's an ancestral wolf instinct, like they're making a den in the snow or whatever. But Buster isn't a wolf, he's a golden retriever who is afraid of the vacuum cleaner. Anyway, he dug a hole right through the upholstery of our old sectional. So we had to go furniture shopping, which is honestly my least favorite thing in the world. We went to this huge warehouse place on a Sunday. The salesman there was wearing the most aggressive cologne I've ever smelled. It smelled like pine needles and gasoline. He kept following us around, standing uncomfortably close, trying to sell us on this modular thing where every piece is separate. He kept saying, "It's a lifestyle choice, brother." Who says that about a couch? We ended up buying it just so we could leave. Getting it delivered was a whole other ordeal, they scratched the front door frame... 

But, uh, what were you asking? Oh, right, feeling hopeless. Yeah, it's just this constant heavy, hollow feeling, like I said. Just dragging myself through the day.
Do you ever find yourself avoiding social interactions or activities you once enjoyed because of feelings of anxiety or overwhelm?

Social stuff? Yeah, definitely. I used to really look forward to things, you know? Like, we had this regular pickup basketball game on Thursday nights, and we'd do bowling sometimes. I even used to love firing up the smoker on the weekends and having people over. I've got this offset smoker, an Oklahoma Joe's, and it takes a lot of work to maintain the temperature. You have to use actual wood splits, not just charcoal. I usually use hickory, sometimes applewood if I'm doing pork shoulder. I actually ordered a cord of hickory from this guy on Facebook Marketplace last fall, and he dumped it right in the middle of my side yard instead of stacking it by the fence like I asked. It took me two whole weekends to move it all by hand, and I found a massive wolf spider in one of the logs. It was the size of a coaster. I tried to hit it with a shovel, but it was so fast, it just disappeared under the deck. Now every time I go out there to grab wood, I'm wearing heavy leather work gloves and kicking the pile first just in case. 

But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, social stuff. Yeah, I used to love doing all that, even music festivals and things. But lately... I don't know. I just find myself canceling on people. Or if I do force myself to show up, I'm just kind of sitting there, going through the motions. I'm not really present. I just want to go home.
Do you think your feelings of hopelessness and anxiety would completely go away if your work situation improved?

Would it go away? I mean... I don't know. Maybe? Like I said earlier, it's just this heavy, gray mood that kind of sticks to me. It follows me from the office, into the car, all the way into the house. Even when nothing is going on, I just sit there feeling hollow. So, maybe if work was better, it wouldn't be so bad. 

But honestly, the car isn't helping my mood either. I drive this 2015 Honda Accord, and the check engine light has been on for, I kid you not, three months. I took it to my mechanic, this guy Sal, who I've been going to for years. He hooked it up to the diagnostic machine and said it was an O2 sensor. He replaced it, charged me two hundred bucks, and the light went off. For exactly one day. The next morning, I'm pulling out of the driveway, and *ding*, there it is again. So I take it back, and Sal says, "Oh, it must be the *other* O2 sensor." There are apparently two of them? Upstream and downstream or something. So he replaces the second one. Another two hundred bucks. Light goes off. Two days later, I'm on the highway, and *ding*. It's back on. At this point, I think Sal is just guessing. I even bought one of those little code readers off Amazon myself so I could see what it's saying. It connects to your phone via Bluetooth. But the app is terrible, it just gives you this string of numbers and letters, like P0420, and when you Google it, it says it could be anything from a loose gas cap to needing a completely new catalytic converter. A new catalytic converter is like a thousand dollars. And with the way people have been stealing them lately, I'm almost afraid to park it anywhere. I saw a video on Nextdoor of a guy sawing one off a Prius in broad daylight...

Wait, sorry. What was the question? Oh, if my mood would improve. Yeah, I mean, I hope so. It's just hard to imagine not feeling this hollow, gray thing all the time, you know?
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt consistently anxious or worried for at least six months?

Anxious for six months? No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had normal worries, like anybody, but not for six months straight. Not like this heavy feeling I have now. 

Speaking of worries, though, my wife has been on this huge health kick lately, and it's honestly making me more stressed out than anything. She watched this documentary on Netflix about microplastics and now she's throwing out all our Tupperware. Perfectly good containers, just straight into the recycling bin. She bought all these glass ones with the snap-on lids, which are fine, I guess, but they weigh a ton. I took some leftover chili to work last week in one of them. I had it in my laptop bag, and I guess the lid wasn't snapped on all the way. Or maybe the glass just didn't seal right, I don't know. But it leaked everywhere. Chili oil all over my charger, in the USB ports of my laptop. It was a disaster. I spent an hour in the breakroom trying to clean it out with Q-tips and rubbing alcohol. And the smell... my whole cubicle smelled like cumin and regret for three days. My coworker, Dave—he sits in the pod next to me—he kept making jokes about opening a taco stand. Dave thinks he's hilarious, but he's really just loud. He has this mechanical keyboard that clacks so loudly I can hear it through my noise-canceling headphones...

Wait, sorry. Six months of anxiety? No, I haven't really had anything like that. Just the normal stuff, until this recent... whatever this is.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried almost every day for the past six months?

Every day for six months? No, I don't think so. I mean, I said no to the six months thing just a minute ago, right? It's just this heavy feeling lately, not like a constant worry for half a year. 

Although, speaking of every day, I have been dealing with this ridiculous issue with my lawn for the past month. Every single morning, I wake up, look out the front window, and there are these huge patches of dead grass. At first, I thought it was grubs. You know, Japanese beetle larvae? They eat the roots from underneath. So I went to Home Depot and bought this massive bag of grub killer. The guy in the garden center, older guy with a name tag that said 'Earl,' told me I had to apply it right before it rained so it would soak into the soil. So I spent my entire Saturday afternoon pushing this spreader back and forth across the yard, trying to beat the storm that was coming in. It rained, the stuff soaked in, and I thought I was good. But a week later, the patches were bigger. So then I set up a trail camera I usually use for hunting, just strapped it to the oak tree in the front yard. And you know what it was? The neighbor's dog. This golden retriever named Buster. Every night at like 2 AM, they just let him out off-leash, and he goes straight to my yard to do his business. The nitrogen in the urine is what's burning the grass. I don't even know how to bring it up to them. They're those neighbors who are almost too friendly, you know? They always wave and want to chat when you're just trying to get the mail...

Wait, sorry. Did you ask about the six months again? Yeah, no, not every day for six months. Just the recent stuff I've been telling you about.
Have you been experiencing this heavy, gray feeling and anxiety for more than six months?

More than six months? Yeah... yeah, definitely more than six. It's actually been going on for about a year and two months now. That's right around when the arguments at home started getting a lot worse. 

Which, honestly, a lot of those arguments started over this stupid kitchen project we tried to take on. We decided to paint the kitchen cabinets ourselves because getting a contractor in to do it was going to be like four grand, and I figured, how hard could it be? I watched all these YouTube tutorials, and this one channel said it was a simple weekend job. Total lie. I went and bought this paint sprayer, one of those high-volume low-pressure ones, and we spent literally three days just taking the doors off and sanding them in the garage. There was fine white dust everywhere. It got into the water heater closet, covered my golf bags, it was a nightmare. 

But the real problem was when I tried to spray the cabinet frames inside the house. I thought I taped off the ceiling well enough, but the plastic sheeting sagged, and I ended up getting "Swiss Coffee" overspray all over the ceiling above the stove. And our ceiling has that textured knockdown finish, so you can't just wipe it off. It's stuck in the grooves. My wife absolutely lost her mind. She wanted to hire a professional to come fix the ceiling and finish the cabinets, which completely defeated the purpose of saving the four grand in the first place. We ended up having this massive blowout in the driveway while I was trying to clean the sprayer nozzle with mineral spirits, and it just kind of set the tone for the whole year... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, so, about a year and two months of feeling this way. Ever since things got really tense at the house.
Have you been experiencing significant anxiety or worry for more than six months?

Anxiety for more than six months? I mean, I feel like I keep saying this, but no, the anxiety part hasn't been going on that long. The heavy feeling, yeah, over a year, but not the constant worry. 

Speaking of worry, though, I've been stressing out about my car lately. I drive this 2018 Accord, and it’s been making this weird rattling noise whenever I hit about 45 miles an hour. Just this low, metallic vibration from the front right side. I took it to my usual mechanic, Tony—he’s got this shop behind the old strip mall on 4th Street. Tony’s a great guy, always gives it to me straight, but his waiting room is like stepping back into 1995. He’s got these faded hunting magazines and a coffee pot that looks like it hasn’t been cleaned since the Clinton administration. Anyway, Tony put it up on the lift, checked the heat shields, the suspension, everything. He couldn't find anything wrong. He told me it might just be a loose piece of trim catching the wind, but it’s driving me crazy. Every time I merge onto the highway, *rattle rattle rattle*. I even tried turning up the radio to drown it out, but then I just started worrying that I was ignoring a bigger problem. Like, what if the wheel bearing is going bad and my tire just flies off while I'm doing 70? 

Wait, sorry, you were asking about the anxiety again, right? Yeah, no, not six months of that. Just the other stuff I mentioned.
Have you been experiencing significant anxiety or worry for most days over the past six months?

Doc, I feel like we're stuck on a loop here. No, I haven't been worrying most days for the past six months. Like I said, I really don't have that constant anxiety thing going on. 

But you know, speaking of being stuck on a loop, that's exactly what it feels like at work lately. I manage a regional sales team, right? And every single quarter, it is the exact same conversation with my reps about logging their client touches in Salesforce. It's like pulling teeth. I have this one guy, Greg. He's a great closer, really good with the clients, but his admin skills are just non-existent. I had to pull him into the glass conference room on Tuesday—the one with the broken blinds that lets the sun hit you right in the eyes at 3 PM. I'm sitting there trying to explain to him that if a call isn't logged, I can't protect his commission if another rep tries to claim the account. And he just starts giving me this endless excuse about how his company iPad keeps freezing whenever he connects to hotel Wi-Fi. 

Which, honestly, he kind of has a point, because our IT department refuses to upgrade our hardware. I've been fighting with the director of operations for six months to get us Surface Pros, but he keeps talking about Q3 budget constraints. He sent out this company-wide email last week with all these pie charts trying to justify the tech freeze, and half the formatting was broken...

Wait, sorry, I'm doing it again. What was the question? Oh, the six months of worrying. Yeah, no, definitely not. I'm just dealing with that heavy feeling I told you about, not the anxiety.
For how long have you been experiencing significant anxiety or worry?

Doc, I... I really don't know how else to say it. There is no "for how long" because I don't have the anxiety. I'm not dealing with significant worry. It's just that heavy, down feeling I told you about. I don't sit around worrying about things. 

Well, actually, the only thing I spent any time worrying about this week was my sprinkler system, but that's just normal homeowner stuff. Zone 3 completely stopped popping up, and the grass was getting all brown near the sidewalk. Right where the HOA president, Gary, walks his golden retriever every single morning. And let me tell you, Gary is an absolute nightmare. He cited me last year because my recycling bin was out like, two hours past the 8 AM deadline on a Tuesday. He actually walks around the neighborhood with a little clipboard. So anyway, I'm out there on Sunday, digging in the mud for like four hours trying to find the solenoid valve box. Turns out this massive oak tree root had just grown straight through the PVC pipe and completely shattered it. I had to drive all the way to Home Depot to get replacement fittings, but they completely rearranged the store. The plumbing aisle used to be right next to the garden center, but now it's all the way over by the lumber, and there was only one guy working in the whole department...

Wait. I'm doing it again, aren't I? Sorry. What I meant was, I don't have a timeline for the anxiety because I don't really have it. Just the heavy feeling.
Has this heavy, gray feeling you've been experiencing lasted for less than 6 months?

No, definitely not less than six months. It's actually been going on for about a year and two months, right around when the arguments at home started getting a lot worse. 

It's crazy, because those arguments really started over the absolute dumbest things. Like, I remember one of the first really bad blowups was just about the garage door opener. We have this Chamberlain Whisper Drive—it's supposed to be super quiet, right? But the safety sensors kept getting misaligned because my wife parks her SUV just a little too close to the track. So I'm out there with a laser level on a Saturday morning, trying to get the little green indicator light to stay solid so the door will actually shut, and she comes out and starts getting on my case about how I'm obsessing over the house instead of spending time with her. And I'm just sitting there like, I'm just trying to make sure the door actually closes so the raccoons don't get into our trash again! 

I don't know if you've noticed, but the raccoons around here are getting huge. One of them literally chewed straight through the heavy-duty plastic lid on my neighbor's bin last month. Just tore right through it like it was a paper plate. The city actually had to send out this big email blast to the whole neighborhood about securing our food waste, but half the people didn't even read it because it went to their spam folders... 

Sorry, I'm rambling again, aren't I? But yeah, to answer your question, it hasn't been less than six months. It's been about a year and two months of this heavy feeling.
